newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BLACKBURN NAME ERIKSSON AS COACH - FROM NEXT SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLACKBURN NAME ERIKSSON AS COACH - FROM NEXT SEASON.

text.p: Sampdoria coach Sven Goran Eriksson was named as the new manager of former English champions Blackburn Rovers on Monday -- although he will not join the club until next July.
Blackburn said caretaker-manager Tony Parkes would remain in charge for the rest of the season.
Blackburn, English champions in 1995 with Kenny Dalglish at the helm, finished seventh last season under manager Ray Harford.

But they made a poor start this season and were in last place when Harford resigned on October 26. Since Parkes took control they have moved up to fourth from bottom but he has repeatedly stressed he was not interested in the job on a long-term basis.
Blackburn did not disclose financial details of Eriksson's three-year contract but the Italian news agency Ansa said it was believed to be worth one million sterling ($1.6 million) a year.

Eriksson expressed pleasure at his appointment on Monday. "I am pleased and honoured to be coming to Blackburn next July, but I am not in a position to give interviews about the next club I will be working with.
"I can only comment on the club I am currently employed by, Sampdoria."
He has an impressive pedigree, starting his coaching career with Gothenberg before having spells with Benfica (twice), Roma and Fiorentina. He is currently in his fifth year with Sampdoria.
The Genoa-based club, eighth in serie A, said he was moving on with their blessing.
"Signor Eriksson is a man of outstanding human and professional qualities. For that reason the club can only wish him the very best of success," a club statement said.
It said Eriksson would continue to play a full part in Sampdoria's current season, a sentiment he echoed.

Blackburn chairman Robert Coar, announcing Eriksson's appointment said: "He has signed a three-year contract which will start on July 1 1997, but if he is released by Sampdoria before that date he will join us immediately.
"In the meantime Tony has the full confidence of everyone at Ewood Park and will remain in charge of team affairs.
"It is not envisaged that there will be any departures of the present staff as a result of this appointment.
"It is some time since Ray Harford left us but we were determined to make the right appointment.

"We are confident we have secured the services of a man of vast experience at a number of top European clubs to underline our ambitions to be a leading club in both the Premiership and also to compete successfully on a regular basis in European competitions."
Coar confirmed that money would be immediately available for team strengthening and hinted that Eriksson would be fully consulted in any deals.
He added: "We have high aspirations as (owner) Jack Walker has said all along and although there is a risk with any manager we don't see it as a gamble."
Parkes, who has pulled Rovers out of the relegation zone in recent weeks, said: "I welcome the appointment with open arms and it's good for the players that the situation has been cleared up.
"I am sure they will be pleased and I am delighted that I'll be staying on also."
